results.question: Which country takes the largest share of Sri Lanka's tea exports?
results.answer: Iraq was the largest importer of Sri Lankan tea in 2024, taking 10.9% of the total export value, which equaled USD 149,621,564 out of a total of USD 1,373,467,019 [1]. Sri Lanka exported tea to 145 different markets that year, reflecting a diversified export strategy with a Herfindahl concentration index of 0.05 [2]. The United Arab Emirates was the fastest-growing market for Sri Lankan tea between 2020 and 2024, with an annual growth rate of 31.6% [3].

results.question: How fast have cinnamon exports grown over the last five years?
results.answer: Cinnamon exports from Sri Lanka have contracted at a rate of 0.2% per year over the last five years, reaching a total export value of USD 214,425,881 in 2024 [5]. Mexico was the largest market for Sri Lankan cinnamon, accounting for 38.4% of the total export value in 2024 [3]. Despite the overall decline, Honduras was the fastest-growing destination for cinnamon exports, with an annual growth rate of 7.7% between 2020 and 2024 [6]. There is no district-level production data available for cinnamon, which limits the ability to analyze production trends or district-specific contributions to exports [2].

results.question: How concentrated are Sri Lanka's rubber export destinations?
